Choice Rules and WARP

Pick bundles yourself in two budget situations. If each situation could have afforded the other’s choice — that violates the Weak Axiom of Revealed Preference (WARP).

x chosen at (p,w), p⋅y≤w⇒y not chosen at (p′,w′) when p′⋅x≤w′x \text{ chosen at } (p,w),\ p\cdot y \le w \Rightarrow y \text{ not chosen at } (p',w') \text{ when } p'\cdot x \le w'x chosen at (p,w), p⋅y≤w⇒y not chosen at (p′,w′) when p′⋅x≤w′

Examples & Exercises

The consumer chose x=(10,50)x = (10, 50)x=(10,50) in situation 1 (p,w)=((1,1),60)(p, w) = ((1,1), 60)(p,w)=((1,1),60) and y=(30,30)y = (30, 30)y=(30,30) in situation 2 (p′,w′)=((2,1),90)(p', w') = ((2,1), 90)(p′,w′)=((2,1),90). Check that both bundles are inside their budgets and decide whether WARP is violated.

p⋅y=60≤60=p⋅x⇒x≿∗yp \cdot y = 60 \le 60 = p \cdot x \quad\Rightarrow\quad x \succsim^* yp⋅y=60≤60=p⋅x⇒x≿∗y
p′⋅x=70≤90=p′⋅y⇒y≿∗xp' \cdot x = 70 \le 90 = p' \cdot y \quad\Rightarrow\quad y \succsim^* xp′⋅x=70≤90=p′⋅y⇒y≿∗x
Show proof
  1. Budget check: p⋅x=10+50=60≤60p \cdot x = 10 + 50 = 60 \le 60p⋅x=10+50=60≤60 and p′⋅y=60+30=90≤90p' \cdot y = 60 + 30 = 90 \le 90p′⋅y=60+30=90≤90 — both sit on their budget lines, so no clamping occurs.
  2. In situation 1, yyy costs p⋅y=30+30=60≤60=p⋅xp \cdot y = 30 + 30 = 60 \le 60 = p \cdot xp⋅y=30+30=60≤60=p⋅x. Since yyy was affordable but xxx was chosen, xxx is revealed preferred to yyy: x≿∗yx \succsim^* yx≿∗y.
  3. In situation 2, xxx costs p′⋅x=20+50=70≤90=p′⋅yp' \cdot x = 20 + 50 = 70 \le 90 = p' \cdot yp′⋅x=20+50=70≤90=p′⋅y. Since xxx was affordable but yyy was chosen, y≿∗xy \succsim^* xy≿∗x. Revealed preference runs both ways between two distinct bundles, so WARP is violated — no preference relation can rationalize this pair of choices.

The consumer chose x=(30,30)x = (30, 30)x=(30,30) in situation 1 and y=(10,70)y = (10, 70)y=(10,70) in situation 2. Show in which single direction revealed preference holds, and verify that WARP holds.

p⋅y=80>60=p⋅xp \cdot y = 80 > 60 = p \cdot xp⋅y=80>60=p⋅x
p′⋅x=90≤90=p′⋅y⇒y≿∗xp' \cdot x = 90 \le 90 = p' \cdot y \quad\Rightarrow\quad y \succsim^* xp′⋅x=90≤90=p′⋅y⇒y≿∗x
Show proof
  1. Budget check: p⋅x=60≤60p \cdot x = 60 \le 60p⋅x=60≤60 and p′⋅y=20+70=90≤90p' \cdot y = 20 + 70 = 90 \le 90p′⋅y=20+70=90≤90 — no clamping.
  2. In situation 1, yyy costs p⋅y=10+70=80>60=p⋅xp \cdot y = 10 + 70 = 80 > 60 = p \cdot xp⋅y=10+70=80>60=p⋅x. Since yyy was not affordable at all, there is no revealed preference for xxx.
  3. In situation 2, xxx costs p′⋅x=60+30=90≤90=p′⋅yp' \cdot x = 60 + 30 = 90 \le 90 = p' \cdot yp′⋅x=60+30=90≤90=p′⋅y, so y≿∗xy \succsim^* xy≿∗x. Revealed preference holds in only one direction, so WARP holds — this data does not contradict utility maximization.
